cases.oracle: Locked util-linux prlimit and independent Python kernel read-back on the same owned-child scenario.
cases.comparison: Exact status and explicit read-back predicates. Dynamic IDs are used only to address owned children or verify the complete expected diagnostic/output before emitting a fixed marker.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 worker.py 0 & child=$!
trap 'kill -TERM "$child" 2>/dev/null; wait "$child" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
/usr/bin/python3 ready.py || exit 90
prlimit --pid "$child" --nofile=32; printf "status=%s\n" "$?"
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import resource,sys;v=resource.prlimit(int(sys.argv[1]),getattr(resource,"RLIMIT_"+sys.argv[2]));print("limits="+",".join("unlimited" if n==resource.RLIM_INFINITY else str(n) for n in v))' "$child" NOFILE

cases.oracle: Locked util-linux prlimit and independent Python kernel read-back on the same owned-child scenario.
cases.comparison: Exact failure status, diagnostic presence, empty setter stdout, and independent kernel read-back.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 worker.py 0 & child=$!
trap 'kill -TERM "$child" 2>/dev/null; wait "$child" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
/usr/bin/python3 ready.py || exit 90
prlimit --pid "$child" --nofile=96:64 > out 2> err; rc=$?; [[ -s err ]] && d=yes || d=no; printf "status=%s diagnostic=%s\n" "$rc" "$d"
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import resource,sys;v=resource.prlimit(int(sys.argv[1]),getattr(resource,"RLIMIT_"+sys.argv[2]));print("limits="+",".join("unlimited" if n==resource.RLIM_INFINITY else str(n) for n in v))' "$child" NOFILE
[[ ! -s out ]] && echo stdout=empty; rm -f out err
